questions.question_text:
The area of a square is 𝑑. What is the area of the circle which has the diagonal of the
square as its diameter?
questions.explaination: For a square of area $d$, the side length is $s = \sqrt{d}$ and its diagonal is $s\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{2d}$. Since this diagonal is the diameter of the circle, the radius is $r = \frac{\sqrt{2d}}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{d}{2}}$. Hence, the area of the circle is $\pi r^2 = \pi \left(\frac{d}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{2}\pi d$.

A six sided unbiased die with four green faces and two red faces is rolled seven times.
Which of the following combinations is the most likely outcome of the experiment?

options.A: Three green faces and four red faces.

Which one of the following is a closed form expression for the generating function of the
sequence {an}, where an = 2n + 3 for all n = 0, 1, 2,… ?
questions.subtopic: Combinatorics: counting, recurrence relations, generating functions
questions.explaination: The generating function is $G(x) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty (2n + 3)x^n = 2\sum_{n=0}^\infty n x^n + 3\sum_{n=0}^\infty x^n$. Using the standard power series $\sum_{n=0}^\infty x^n = \frac{1}{1-x}$ and $\sum_{n=0}^\infty n x^n = \frac{x}{(1-x)^2}$, we obtain $G(x) = \frac{2x}{(1-x)^2} + \frac{3(1-x)}{(1-x)^2} = \frac{3 - x}{(1-x)^2}$.

numbered 1 to 6. The person with the lower number wins. In case of a tie, they roll the dice

Consider a system with 3 processes that share 4 instances of the same resource type. Each
process can request a maximum of 𝐾 instances. Resource instances can be requested and
released only one at a time. The largest value of 𝐾 that will always avoid deadlock is ____.

questions.explaination: Using the law of total probability, the probability of high temperature in Delhi is $P(H_D) = 0.2(0.40) + 0.5(0.10) + 0.3(0.01) = 0.08 + 0.05 + 0.003 = 0.133$. By Bayes' theorem, $P(H_G \mid H_D) = \frac{P(H_G \cap H_D)}{P(H_D)} = \frac{0.08}{0.133} \approx 0.6015$, which falls in the range $0.60$ to $0.62$.

questions.question_text:
The number of possible min-heaps containing each value from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}exactly once

questions.subtopic: Trees, binary search trees, binary heaps
questions.explaination: In a min-heap of 7 elements, the root must contain the minimum element (1). The left subtree has size 3 and the right subtree has size 3. Choosing 3 elements for the left subtree from the remaining 6 elements can be done in $\binom{6}{3} = 20$ ways. A 3-element min-heap has $\binom{2}{1} = 2$ valid configurations. Hence, total valid min-heaps $= 20 \times 2 \times 2 = 80$.

questions.question_text:
The instruction pipeline of a RISC processor has the following stages: Instruction Fetch (IF),
Instruction Decode (ID), Operand Fetch (OF), Perform Operation (PO) and Writeback (WB).
The IF, ID, OF and WB stages take 1 clock cycle each for every instruction. Consider a
sequence of 100 instructions. In the PO stage, 40 instructions take 3 clock cycles each, 35
instructions take 2 clock cycles each, and the remaining 25 instructions take 1 clock cycle
each. Assume that there are no data hazards and no control hazards.

The number of clock cycles required for completion of execution of the sequence of
instructions is ______.
questions.explaination: For 100 instructions in a 5-stage pipeline without branch delays, ideal cycles $= 5 + (100 - 1) = 104$. The PO stage causes pipeline stalls when operand evaluation takes extra cycles: 40 instructions require 3 cycles (2 extra cycles $\implies 40 \times 2 = 80$ stall cycles) and 35 instructions require 2 cycles (1 extra cycle $\implies 35 \times 1 = 35$ stall cycles). Total clock cycles $= 104 + 80 + 35 = 219$.
questions.question_text_latex: The instruction pipeline of a RISC processor has five stages: Instruction Fetch (IF), Instruction Decode (ID), Perform Operation (PO), Operand Read (OR), and Write Back (WB). Each stage takes 1 clock cycle except PO. Assuming no memory stalls or branch delays, the total number of clock cycles to execute the 100 instructions is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.

questions.question_text:
A processor has 16 integer registers (R0, R1, .. , R15) and 64 floating point registers (F0,
F1,… , F63). It uses a 2-byte instruction format. There are four categories of instructions:
Type-1, Type-2, Type-3, and Type-4. Type-1 category consists of four instructions, each
with 3 integer register operands (3Rs). Type-2 category consists of eight instructions, each
with 2 floating point register operands (2Fs). Type-3 category consists of fourteen
instructions, each with one integer register operand and one floating point register operand
(1R+1F). Type-4 category consists of N instructions, each with a floating point register
operand (1F).

The maximum value of N is __________.
questions.explaination: A 16-bit instruction space has $2^{16} = 65536$ encodings. Type-1: 4 instructions with $3 \times 4\text{-bit}$ registers consume $4 \times 2^{12} = 16384$. Type-2: 8 instructions with $2 \times 6\text{-bit}$ registers consume $8 \times 2^{12} = 32768$. Type-3: 14 instructions with 4-bit and 6-bit registers consume $14 \times 2^{10} = 14336$. Remaining encodings $= 65536 - (16384 + 32768 + 14336) = 2048$. Each Type-4 instruction uses one 6-bit register ($2^6 = 64$ encodings). Thus, maximum $N = 2048 / 64 = 32$.

questions.question_text:
Consider a storage disk with 4 platters (numbered as 0, 1, 2 and 3), 200 cylinders (numbered
as 0, 1, … , 199), and 256 sectors per track (numbered as 0, 1, … , 255). The following 6
disk requests of the form [sector number, cylinder number, platter number] are received by
the disk controller at the same time:
[120, 72, 2] , [180, 134, 1] , [60, 20, 0] , [212, 86, 3] , [56, 116, 2] , [118, 16, 1]

Currently the head is positioned at sector number 100 of cylinder 80, and is moving towards
higher cylinder numbers. The average power dissipation in moving the head over 100
cylinders is 20 milliwatts and for reversing the direction of the head movement once is 15
milliwatts. Power dissipation associated with rotational latency and switching of head
between different platters is negligible.

The total power consumption in milliwatts to satisfy all of the above disk requests using the
Shortest Seek Time First disk scheduling algorithm is _______.
questions.explaination: Using Shortest Seek Time First (SSTF) starting at cylinder 80: closest is 86 (diff 6, upward), then 72 (diff 14, downward $\implies$ reversal 1), then 116 (diff 44, upward $\implies$ reversal 2), then 134 (diff 18, upward), then 20 (diff 114, downward $\implies$ reversal 3), and finally 16 (diff 4, downward). Total cylinder distance $= 6 + 14 + 44 + 18 + 114 + 4 = 200$. Head movement power $= 200 \times 0.2\text{ mW} = 40\text{ mW}$. Direction reversals $= 3 \times 15\text{ mW} = 45\text{ mW}$. Total power consumed $= 40 + 45 = 85\text{ mW}$.

The read/write head is currently at cylinder 80 and moving towards higher cylinder numbers. The SSTF algorithm is used. questions.question_text:
Consider an IP packet with a length of 4,500 bytes that includes a 20-byte IPv4 header and
a 40-byte TCP header. The packet is forwarded to an IPv4 router that supports a Maximum
Transmission Unit (MTU) of 600 bytes. Assume that the length of the IP header in all the
outgoing fragments of this packet is 20 bytes. Assume that the fragmentation offset value
stored in the first fragment is 0.

The fragmentation offset value stored in the third fragment is _______.
questions.subtopic: Fragmentation and IP addressing, IPv4, CIDR notation
questions.explaination: Total payload to fragment $= 4500 - 20 = 4480$ bytes. With $\text{MTU} = 600$, maximum payload per fragment must be a multiple of 8: $\lfloor (600 - 20) / 8 \rfloor \times 8 = 72 \times 8 = 576$ bytes. Fragment 1 carries bytes 0 to 575 (offset 0). Fragment 2 carries bytes 576 to 1151 (offset $576/8 = 72$). Fragment 3 carries bytes 1152 onwards, so its fragment offset field is $\frac{1152}{8} = 144$.

The packet is forwarded across an IP network with an MTU of 600 bytes. The value of the fragment offset field in the third fragment (in 8-byte units) is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.
